summary: The Save Our Shrimpers Act requires the Secretary of the Treasury to direct US Executive Directors at international financial institutions to oppose any funding for shrimp farming, processing, or export projects in borrowing countries, subject to a national-interest waiver and a 7-year sunset.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs US representatives at international financial institutions to oppose loans or assistance for foreign shrimp projects. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any US federal spending, so it has no bearing on government spending.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, or revenue measures.
No provisions relate to healthcare systems, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, or border policy.
No provisions relate to reproductive health or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military or defense budgets.

Shrimp aquaculture can involve environmental harms such as mangrove loss, but the bill's purpose is domestic industry protection rather than environmental regulation. Any environmental effect is incidental and not addressed in the text.
No provisions relate to welfare programs or social safety-net spending.
No provisions relate to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions relate to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions relate to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.

The bill instructs US directors to block international financing for foreign shrimp production, processing, and exports. This is a targeted protectionist measure intended to shield domestic shrimp producers from foreign competition financed by multilateral institutions.
No provisions address deficits, debt levels, or fiscal targets.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections.

The bill requires opposition to financial assistance from international financial institutions for specific shrimp-related projects in borrowing countries. This constitutes a limited restriction on certain forms of multilateral development assistance.
No provisions relate to voting access or election administration.
No provisions relate to technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions relate to labor rights or union power.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
